profile.headline: Back-end engineer by trade, my professional work deals with mostly services and workflows at large scale while I also moonlight as a full-stack engineer for hobby projects to keep my front-end skills practiced,

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
As of 2024, I've only worked on two teams at Amazon.

From joining right out of college to 2017, I worked on the team that develops and maintains the page assembly engine for Amazon retail website (amazon.com). The software's core libraries are written in C++ while the pages are written in Perl/Mason with Apache servers under the hood. The software was constantly under deprecation efforts to be replaced with more modern website frameworks that are friendlier to recruitment (it's difficult to attract website engineers to work on Perl/Mason code while the all the hottest technologies are in Node - React, Angular, etc.). But the fact remains that the custom-made battle-tested production-hardened page assembly just does too good of a job that by the time I left the team, the piece of software still renders ~65% of all amazon.com traffic.

In 2017, I joined the team under Amazon's Builder Tools organisation that owns the dozens of services that together facilitate millions of software deployments per day for internal Amazon services. I chose this team because of the huge and immediate impact they have. I like to be able to talk to my customers directly, listen to their concerns and feature requests, and then able to design, lead, and/or, carry out plans to meet those goals. I am most fond of a project that, as part of an umbrella of projects across several teams, eventually brought container deployments to Amazon internal services. Another project that is smaller in scope but no less impressive is migrating a very heavily-used Amazon internal website from a mixture of Perl/Mason and Ruby on Rails pages to just ReactJS. Even though the professional work doesn't involve a lot of front-end coding, I keep my hands busy with projects that allow me to stay in touch with the latest website technologies.

positions.title: Undergraduate Assistant
positions.description: There were two parts to my job: first, I had to prepare some homework assignments, as well as grade them for four three with two professors. Along with that, I was involved with Miami's HIVE research efforts; my specific assignment was to write the C/C++ API that acts as a bridge between the laser device and other code that needs to get the range data from such hardware.

positions.title: Student Aide
positions.description: I helped prepare and teach an introductory graduate course to programming. I had to refit an easier course meant for undergraduate students to a graduate-level course, changing the original Java assignments to C/C++ projects.

projects.title: Breakthrough AI Player
projects.description: In this project, we were tasked with implementing an AI player for the board game Breakthrough. The AI player is a timed iterative deepening alpha-beta search (it is a conglomerate of three concepts). More updates to come as the project is being completed.

projects.title: Droid-Lazr
projects.description: Droid-Lazr is the product to the class "Introduction to Computer Graphics." It is coded entirely in C++ using OpenGL with graphics assets done by collaborators. Because the class was not game-oriented, the "game" is more of a technical demonstration than a working game.
